newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Savage sees lift in U.S. zinc premiums.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Savage sees lift in U.S. zinc premiums.

text.p: Spot zinc premiums in the U.S. for Special High Grade brand are poised to climb by a few cents to around eight or nine cents a pound due to an emerging supply pinch, the general manager of marketing for Savage Resources Ltd, which operates Savage Zinc Co of the U.S., said on Friday.
This compares with long-term contract premiums of closer to five or six cents a pound over the LME price, Boyer said.
Little SGH zinc existed in LME warehouses beyond that produced by Spanish zinc company Asturiana de Zinc SA, much of which was now controlled by an international trading company, Boyer said.
Late last year, Asturiana said it had gradually liquidated its zinc position on the LME through Swiss trader Glencore International in 1996.
U.S. steel mills look to purchase SHG zinc, Boyer said.
Less pricy high grade-type zinc produced in places including the Commonwealth of Independent States usually trades at a discount of four to five cents a pound to the LME, he said.
Boyer said he sees the current contango in the market narrowing and possibly a backwardation eventually emerging as nearby supplies tighten.
Boyer said the U.S. was destined to remain a net importer of large quantities of zinc, most of which would come from Canada.
"There is no question the U.S. will be a major importer of metal for years to come," Boyer told the symposium.
Boyer said a A$10 million study into expanding Savage's 105,000-tonnes-a-year zinc refinery in Clarksville, Tenn, by 175,000 tonnes would be completed by the end of 1997.
Robust demand for zinc reflected in healthy market premiums, relatively cheap labor and energy and U.S. dollar-denominated sales all supported the case for an expansion, Boyer said.
Growth in consumption of zinc in the U.S. will lift consumption slightly to 1.32 million tonnes in 1998 from a forecast 1.3 million this year.
This year scope existed for imports to the U.S. of 888,00 tonnes, Savage figures show.
